Though this appeal is listed for admission, with the consent of learned counsel for the parties, it is taken up for final disposal.

2. The claimant-injured is before this Court dissatisfied with the quantum of compensation awarded under judgment and award dated 7.9.2017 in M.V.C. No.2836/2016 on the file of learned IX Addl.
District and Sessions Judge & Member, Addl. MACT, Belagavi (for short, 'Tribunal'), praying for enhancement of compensation.
3.
Heard learned counsel Smt.Shaila Bellikatti for the appellant and Sri.Girish C Kattimani, learned counsel for respondent-Insurance Company and perused the appeal papers along with original records.

4. The appellant/claimant filed a claim petition under Section 166 of the M.V. Act claiming compensation for the injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident that occurred on 13.06.2016 involving Motorcycle bearing registration No.KA- 48/J-3011 and Maruti Swift Car bearing registration No.KA-22- C-2348.

It is stated that the appellant/claimant was aged 51 NC:
2024:KHC-D:7684-DB years as on the date of the accident and was a medical practitioner, earning more than Rs.30,000/- per month.
5.
On issuance of notice, respondent-Insurance Company appeared through its counsel and filed statement of objections denying the entire averments made in the claim petition.
It was contended that due to negligence on the part of rider of the motorcycle, accident took place and the rider was not having valid and effective driving license as on the date of the accident.
Hence, sought for dismissal of the claim petition.

The claimant in support of his case examined himself as PW1 and examined Doctor as PW2 apart from marking documents as Exs.P1 to P22.
Respondents did not examine any witness but marked insurance policy as Ex.R1.

The Tribunal on appreciation of material on record, awarded total compensation of Rs.1,63,520/- with interest at 6% per annum from the date of petition till realization on the following heads:
Pain & suffering Rs.30,000/-
Loss of future earnings Rs.73,920/-
Medical & incidental expenses Rs.53,600/-
Food, transport, attendant charges including loss of income during hospital Rs. 6,000/-
 -----------------
 Total Rs.1,63,520/-
 -----------------
 NC: 2024:KHC-D:7684-DB 7.

While awarding the above compensation, the Tribunal assessed notional income of the claimant/injured at Rs.8,000/- per month, applied multiplier of 11 and assessed whole body disability of the injured at 7%.
Not being satisfied with the quantum of compensation, the claimant is before this Court praying for enhancement of compensation.

8. Smt. Shaila Bellikatti, learned counsel for the appellant/injured would submit that notional income of the claimant assessed by the Tribunal at Rs.8,000/- per month is on the lower side,
inasmuch as he was a Medical Practitioner and earning Rs.30,000/- per month. Learned counsel submits that to establish the income of the injured, Ex.P14-Income tax returns has been produced,
however, the Tribunal failed to consider the same.

She further submits that the Tribunal committed an error in assessing whole body disability of the injured at 7%, which is contrary to the evidence of doctor-PW2, who deposed that the claimant has suffered permanent physical disability at 37% to left lower limb.
Thus, she submits that the Tribunal ought to have assessed whole body disability on the higher side.
It is further submitted that no compensation has been awarded on the head of loss of amenities and the award NC: 2024:KHC-D:7684-DB of compensation on the other heads are also on the lower side.
Thus, she prays for enhancement of compensation by allowing the appeal.

9. Per contra, Sri.Girish C Kattimani, learned counsel for respondent No.2-Insurance Company contends that in the absence of cogent and acceptable evidence to prove the income of the injured,
the Tribunal has rightly assessed the notional income at Rs.8,000/- per moth.
He further submits that the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal is just and proper, which needs no interference.
Thus, he prays for dismissal of the appeal.

10. Having heard the learned counsel for the parties and on perusal of the appeal papers along with original records, the only point that would arise for consideration in this appeal is, whether the Nazeerehussain S/O. sentences.text: appellant/claimant would be entitled for enhanced compensation?
11. Answer to the above point would be in the 'affirmative' for the following reasons.

12. The occurrence of the accident that took place on 13.06.2016 involving Motorcycle bearing registration No.KA- 48/J-3011 and Maruti Swift Car bearing registration No.KA-22- NC:
2024:KHC-D:7684-DB C-2348, resulting in injuries to the claimant is not in dispute in this appeal.
The claimant is before this Court praying for enhancement of compensation.
The Tribunal assessed notional income of the claimant at Rs.8,000/- per month.
It is stated that the claimant was a Medical Practitioner and earning Rs.30,000/- per month.
To substantiate the said contention, the claimant has produced Ex.P14-Income Tax return, which discloses gross income of the injured at Rs.1,63,367/- for the Assessment Year 2015-16.
However, no income returns prior to 2015-16 or subsequent year is placed on record.
Hence, Ex.P14 cannot be the basis to assess the income, since no other cogent material whatsoever is placed on record to substantiate the avocation and earning of the injured.

In the absence of any documentary evidence to establish the avocation and income of the injured, this Court and Lok Adalath while settling the accidental claims of the year 2016 would normally assess notional income at Rs.8,750/- per month, taking note of the income chart prepared by KSLSA based on various factors including the minimum wage fixed.

Therefore, in the instant case also, in the absence of any corroborative document to establish the income of the NC:
2024:KHC-D:7684-DB injured, we are of the opinion that it would be just and appropriate for us to determine notional income of the injured at Rs.8,750/- p.m., taking note of the income chart prepared by KSLSA and also the minimum wage fixed.
13. Ex.P6 is the Wound Certificate of the claimant and Ex.P20 is the Disability Certificate.
A perusal of Ex.P6 and Ex.P20 would disclose that the claimant/injured sustained fracture of lower 1/3rd of Tibia and Fibula to left leg.
In support of his case, the claimant examined PW2-Doctor, who has deposed in his evidence that the injured/claimant has suffered 37% permanent physical disability to the left lower limb.
However, the Tribunal assessed functional disability of the claimant at 7% to the whole body, which in our view is on the lower side.
It is settled position of law that 1/3rd of disability to a particular limb is to be taken as disability to the whole body.
If functional disability of the injured to left lower limb is taken at 37% as stated by PW2-doctor, 1/3rd of which would be 12%.
Thus, we are of the opinion that it is appropriate to re-assess the disability of the claimant at 12% to the whole body as against 7% assessed by the Tribunal.
There is no dispute with regard to the age of the claimant i.e. 51 years and proper multiplier of 11 to the age of the claimant.
Thus, the claimant would be entitled to compensation on the head of loss of future earnings at Rs.1,38,600/- (Rs.8,750 X 12 (months) x 11(multiplier) x 12/100 (disability).
15. The Tribunal awarded a sum of Rs.30,000/- on the head of pain and suffering, which is on the lower side.
Considering the nature of injuries and also fracture sustained by the claimant, the amount awarded on the said head is enhanced to Rs.40,000/-.
No compensation has been awarded towards loss of amenities.

16. The Tribunal awarded a meager sum of Rs.6,000/- towards food, nourishment and attendant charges and therefore, the same is enhanced to Rs.10,000/-.
